{"path":"C:/Users/Kevyn Lucas/Downloads/PROMPT_COLETA_INSTAGRAM_AGOSTO_2026.txt","content":"Você é um agente de automação responsável por concluir, com evidência, um relatório de métricas do Instagram.

OBJETIVO
Coletar TODOS os posts publicados pelo perfil @acirvoficial entre 2026-08-01 00:00:00 e 2026-08-31 23:59:59, no fuso America/Sao_Paulo, abrindo cada publicação individualmente e usando o botão “Ver insights”. Criar/atualizar uma planilha Excel na pasta Downloads.

REGRAS ABSOLUTAS
1. Fonte primária: cada URL individual do post e a tela individual aberta por “Ver insights”. Não use apenas o painel agregado do Instagram.
2. Inclua somente posts cujo perfil seja exatamente @acirvoficial e cuja data exibida na publicação esteja em agosto de 2026. Não inclua posts marcados, reposts, anúncios de terceiros ou posts de outros perfis.
3. Não filtre pelo conteúdo da legenda, tipo de mídia ou desempenho. Inclua foto, vídeo, carrossel e reel do próprio perfil.
4. Não invente, estime, arredonde ou copie métricas de outro post. Se uma métrica não aparecer, deixe a célula vazia e registre o nome em “metricas_ausentes”.
5. Não trate “Ver insights” sem dados visíveis como sucesso. Aguarde o carregamento, confirme a tela/modal e capture os valores efetivamente exibidos.
6. Nunca exponha, salve ou repita senhas, tokens, cookies ou códigos de autenticação. Se aparecerem em texto/log, substitua por [REDACTED].
7. Não altere curtidas, comentários, posts, configurações, anúncios ou qualquer dado da conta.

PROCEDIMENTO DETERMINÍSTICO
A. Preparação
- Abra uma sessão autenticada do Instagram. Se houver tela de login, CAPTCHA, verificação, autorização ou pedido de senha, pare e solicite intervenção humana; não tente adivinhar credenciais.
- Abra https://www.instagram.com/acirvoficial/.
- Role o grid até carregar posts suficientemente antigos para cobrir 01/08/2026 a 31/08/2026. Capture todos os links únicos /acirvoficial/p/ e /acirvoficial/reel/.
- Para cada miniatura, leia a data no atributo alt, no link, na página individual ou no elemento time. Registre a evidência da data. Continue rolando até que o grid passe de 01/08/2026; pare somente quando o próximo conteúdo for anterior a 01/08/2026 ou não houver mais posts.
- Elimine duplicatas por shortcode. Ordene por data decrescente. Gere a lista fechada de URLs antes de coletar métricas.

B. Processamento de CADA publicação
Para cada URL, sem pular nenhuma:
1. Navegue diretamente para a URL.
2. Confirme que o cabeçalho/autor é @acirvoficial.
3. Capture a legenda completa, shortcode/URL, tipo de mídia e data exata exibida.
4. Localize o controle com texto/aria-label “Ver insights” e clique nele.
5. Aguarde até 5 segundos; se necessário, aguarde em incrementos de 1 segundo até 15 segundos. Confirme que os dados de Insights apareceram em modal, painel ou página.
6. Leia todo o texto e todos os elementos estruturados da tela de Insights; role o modal/painel até o fim. Não capture somente o primeiro bloco.
7. Registre cada métrica com seu nome original e valor original, incluindo, quando exibidos: visualizações, alcance/contas alcançadas, visualizadores, curtidas, comentários, compartilhamentos, salvamentos, interações, contas engajadas, seguidores/não seguidores, origem das visualizações, atividade do perfil, visitas ao perfil, cliques/toques em links, toques no endereço comercial, novos seguidores, respostas e qualquer outra métrica presente.
8. Preserve percentuais e categorias separadamente. Preserve números como números quando forem claramente números; mantenha valores como “1,2 mil” em uma coluna bruta e, somente se for inequívoco, uma coluna numérica normalizada.
9. Feche o modal ou navegue para o próximo post. Nunca reutilize referência/selector depois de uma navegação sem obter um novo snapshot.
10. Grave o registro imediatamente em arquivo intermediário para permitir retomada após falha.

C. Falhas e retomada
- Se “Ver insights” não abrir, tente novamente somente após novo snapshot e espera; depois tente recarregar a publicação uma vez.
- Se ainda falhar, registre status_insights=NAO_ABERTO, erro e timestamp; não invente valores. Continue para o próximo post.
- Se o post carregar sem data confiável, status_data=NAO_CONFIRMADA e não o conte como concluído.
- Se a sessão expirar, pare e peça login humano; preserve o progresso já salvo.
- Ao reiniciar, leia a planilha/intermediário existente e processe somente URLs ainda não concluídas ou com status de erro.

PLANILHA
Criar o arquivo:
C:\Users\Kevyn Lucas\Downloads\instagram_acirvoficial_insights_agosto_2026.xlsx

Use estas abas:
1. “Posts” — uma linha por publicação, com estas colunas mínimas:
   url, shortcode, data_publicacao, hora_publicacao, tipo_midia, legenda, status_data, status_insights, erro, coletado_em, metricas_ausentes
   e uma coluna para CADA métrica encontrada, usando nomes estáveis em snake_case.
2. “Metricas_brutas” — formato longo, uma linha por métrica: shortcode, url, data_publicacao, secao_insights, nome_metrica_original, valor_original, valor_numerico_se_seguro, observacao.
3. “Controle” — perfil, período inicial, período final, total_de_urls_encontradas, total_de_posts_no_periodo, total_processados, total_com_insights, total_sem_insights, total_com_data_nao_confirmada, URLs com erro, data/hora da última execução e observações.

A planilha deve ter cabeçalho congelado, autofiltro, largura legível, datas em formato ISO YYYY-MM-DD e valores brutos preservados. Não apague os 8 registros já existentes no arquivo se eles corresponderem a posts de agosto; valide-os e complete os faltantes.

VALIDAÇÃO OBRIGATÓRIA ANTES DE FINALIZAR
1. Recalcule programaticamente a lista de URLs únicas do período a partir do perfil e compare com a planilha.
2. total_de_posts_no_periodo deve ser igual ao número de URLs únicas confirmadas entre 01 e 31 de agosto.
3. Cada URL confirmada deve aparecer exatamente uma vez na aba Posts.
4. Para cada linha, confirme autor, data, shortcode e status_insights.
5. Confirme que a aba Metricas_brutas contém todas as métricas visíveis, sem remover métricas que apareceram apenas em um post.
6. Abra o XLSX novamente com uma biblioteca de leitura e verifique que não está corrompido, que há dados e que as contagens batem.
7. Faça uma segunda checagem no grid para garantir que não ficaram posts de agosto sem URL/processamento.
8. Só declare “completo” se todos os posts confirmados tiverem sido processados. Caso contrário, declare claramente: encontrados, processados, concluídos, pendentes, sem Insights e erros.

ENTREGA FINAL
Informe somente resultados verificáveis:
- caminho absoluto do XLSX;
- total de posts confirmados no período;
- total processado;
- total com Insights capturados;
- total sem Insights e respectivos shortcodes;
- total com erro/data não confirmada;
- confirmação de que o arquivo foi reaberto e validado;
- lista curta de limitações reais.
Não diga que terminou se a validação de contagem ou a captura individual de Insights não tiver sido comprovada.
"}

# Instagram Post Metrics Reporting

Collect metrics from recent Instagram posts and deliver a verified spreadsheet.
Use this when the user wants the latest N posts from a profile summarized in Excel,
especially for professional/business accounts where post-level insights are visible on web.

## When to Use

- The user asks for a spreadsheet of the latest Instagram posts.
- The task is to capture post metrics from a professional account and organize them.
- The output must land in `Downloads` or another user-facing folder and be verified.

## Prerequisites

- The user is already authenticated in Instagram Web.
- The target account is accessible from the current session.
- If insights require a professional/business login or a permission wall appears, stop and ask the user to authenticate instead of guessing credentials.
- For `.xlsx` output, use Python + `openpyxl`.

## Core Workflow

1. **Confirm access first**
   - Open Instagram Web and verify you can reach the target profile.
   - Confirm the account is the intended one before collecting data.

2. **Find the complete owned-post set**
   - Prefer direct profile navigation.
   - Identify post URLs from links containing `/p/` or `/reel/` on the profile page.
   - When the request covers a whole year, date range, or says “all posts”, repeatedly force a downward scroll on the profile grid/feed so Instagram has time to lazy-load older posts. Continue persistent scrolling until several consecutive scrolls add no new owned-post URLs, or until posts clearly pass the requested start date.
   - After each scroll batch, harvest and deduplicate the newly loaded URLs; do not rely only on the first viewport.
   - Filter by the requested date range and verify chronological coverage before opening posts. Do not stop at “some recent posts”.

3. **Open each post directly**
   - Navigate to the post URL itself.
   - Once loaded, inspect both the visible page text and DOM-extracted text.

4. **Prefer text extraction over brittle clicking**
   - If `browser_snapshot` is sparse or misses rendered content, use `browser_console` to read `document.body.innerText` and relevant metadata.
   - On some Instagram post pages, the insight metrics are already present in the inline rendered text even when clicking **Ver insights** fails.
   - Before retrying clicks, inspect the current text; do not assume the metric is unavailable just because the snapshot is empty.

5. **Normalize metrics carefully**
   - Capture the post identity: URL, shortcode, publication time text, timestamp when available, caption snippet.
   - Capture every visible metric with its label, not just headline totals.
   - Preserve raw extracted lines in addition to normalized columns so later review can reconcile ambiguities.
   - Prefer explicitly labeled insight values over public social proof text like “Curtido por X e outras Y pessoas”.

6. **Build the workbook**
   - Create at least these sheets:
     - `Resumo`: one row per post with normalized fields.
     - `RawInsights`: raw label/value lines for auditability.
     - `Observacoes`: collection notes, caveats, timestamp, and source profile.
   - Keep the sheet human-readable: bold header row, freeze panes, autofilter, wrapped text for captions/notes.

7. **Verify the artifact**
   - Re-open the workbook with `openpyxl.load_workbook`.
   - Confirm the file exists, sheet names are correct, and row counts are plausible.
   - Only then tell the user it is ready.

## Recommended Extraction Pattern

When Instagram’s structured snapshot is too thin, extract with browser JS:

- `document.body.innerText` for visible metrics and labels.
- `meta[property="og:description"]` / `og:title` for post summary text.
- `time` element for machine-readable post datetime when present.
- Link harvesting from the profile page to enumerate recent posts.

## Pitfalls

- **Sparse snapshots are not proof of missing data.** Instagram often renders useful text that the accessibility snapshot omits.
- **“Ver insights” may fail to click even when insights are already visible inline.** Inspect page text before retrying.
- **Metric labels vary slightly.** Preserve raw labels and map them conservatively instead of forcing guesses.
- **Infinite-scroll grids are incomplete by default, but scrolling must be bounded.** For whole-period requests, scroll persistently in batches and deduplicate after each batch. Stop as soon as the first post outside the requested year/period is detected, then make only a small confirmation scroll (for example, one additional batch) to verify the boundary. Never scroll to the end of the profile or use an unbounded timer. A single viewport, a single scroll, or the initial HTML is not evidence of completeness.
- **Do not infer absent metrics.** If a metric is not visible, leave it blank and note that in `Observacoes`.
- **Authentication blockers are real blockers.** Stop for user login rather than faking progress.

## Verification Checklist

- Target profile confirmed.
- Exactly the requested number of recent posts collected.
- Workbook created in the requested folder.
- Workbook re-opened successfully.
- Final reply includes the exact output path.

## References

- See `references/field-mapping.md` for a compact mapping of common Instagram insight labels to spreadsheet columns and collection notes.

# Xlsx Skill

Work with Excel .xlsx workbooks using Python and openpyxl: build styled
multi-sheet workbooks with formulas and charts, inspect or dump existing
files, edit cells and structure, and convert to/from CSV. All helper
scripts are argparse CLIs that print JSON and use explicit UTF-8 I/O.

## When to Use

- Creating .xlsx reports: multiple sheets, number formats, styling,
  merged cells, freeze panes, autofilter, conditional formatting,
  charts, data-validation dropdowns, native Excel tables, defined
  names, hyperlinks, cell notes, sheet protection.
- Reading a workbook: sheet inventory, dumping data as JSON or CSV,
  listing formulas vs cached values, notes, defined names, tables.
- Editing existing files: set cells, append rows, insert/delete
  rows/columns (reference-aware via `xlsx_restructure.py`),
  copy/rename sheets, tables, names, notes, protection.
- Recalculating formulas headlessly via LibreOffice
  (`xlsx_recalc.py`).
- CSV interop with type inference and non-UTF-8 encodings.
- Not for the legacy .xls binary format (use LibreOffice to convert
  first: `soffice --headless --convert-to xlsx old.xls`).

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.10+ with `openpyxl` (`pip install openpyxl`). No other
  third-party packages are needed; everything else is stdlib.
- Optional: LibreOffice (`soffice`) for headless recalculation or
  format conversion.

## How to Run

Run the helper scripts with the `terminal` tool from this skill's
`scripts/` directory (every script supports `--help`):

```bash
python scripts/xlsx_create.py spec.json report.xlsx   # build from JSON spec
python scripts/xlsx_read.py report.xlsx --sheets      # inventory
python scripts/xlsx_read.py report.xlsx --json --sheet Data
python scripts/xlsx_read.py report.xlsx --formulas
python scripts/xlsx_edit.py report.xlsx --sheet Data --set B2=42 --recalc
python scripts/xlsx_restructure.py report.xlsx --sheet Data --insert-rows 3:2
python scripts/xlsx_recalc.py report.xlsx
python scripts/csv_to_xlsx.py data.csv out.xlsx --encoding utf-8
python scripts/xlsx_to_csv.py report.xlsx out.csv --sheet Data
```

Author the JSON spec with `write_file`, inspect script JSON output with
`read_file` or directly from stdout.

## Quick Reference

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Create workbook from spec | `xlsx_create.py spec.json out.xlsx` |
| Sheet names + dimensions | `xlsx_read.py f.xlsx --sheets` |
| Dump sheet as JSON | `xlsx_read.py f.xlsx --json --sheet S` |
| Dump sheet as CSV | `xlsx_read.py f.xlsx --csv --out d.csv` |
| List formulas + cached values | `xlsx_read.py f.xlsx --formulas` |
| Set a cell / formula | `xlsx_edit.py f.xlsx --set "A1==SUM(B:B)"` |
| Append a row | `xlsx_edit.py f.xlsx --append '[1,"x",true]'` |
| Insert 2 rows, refs NOT shifted | `xlsx_edit.py f.xlsx --insert-rows 3:2` |
| Insert 2 rows, refs shifted | `xlsx_restructure.py f.xlsx --insert-rows 3:2` |
| Delete a column, refs shifted | `xlsx_restructure.py f.xlsx --delete-cols B` |
| Create a native table | `xlsx_edit.py f.xlsx --add-table Sales:A1:C9` |
| Append inside a table | `--table-append 'Sales=["West",5]'` |
| List tables | `xlsx_edit.py f.xlsx --list-tables` |
| Defined names | `--define-name "Rates='Data'!$B$2:$B$9"` / `--delete-name Rates` / `xlsx_read.py f.xlsx --names` |
| Hyperlink | `--hyperlink "A1=https://example.com|Docs"` |
| Cell note | `--note "B2=Check this|Reviewer"`; read via `xlsx_read.py f.xlsx --notes` |
| Protect sheet (see Pitfalls) | `--protect your-password --unlock B2:B9` |
| Recalculate via LibreOffice | `xlsx_recalc.py f.xlsx` |
| Copy / rename sheet | `--copy-sheet Src:New --rename-sheet Old:New` |
| Force recalc on open | `xlsx_edit.py f.xlsx --recalc` |
| CSV -> styled xlsx | `csv_to_xlsx.py in.csv out.xlsx` |
| xlsx -> CSV | `xlsx_to_csv.py f.xlsx out.csv --encoding utf-8` |

## Procedure

1. **Create**: write a JSON spec (schema documented in
   `xlsx_create.py --help` and its docstring). Each sheet supports
   `rows` (scalars or styled cell objects), sparse `cells` overrides,
   `column_widths`, `row_heights`, `merges`, `freeze_panes`,
   `autofilter`, `conditional_formats` (cell_is rules and color
   scales), `charts` (bar/line/pie from cell ranges),
   `validations` (list dropdowns), `tables` (native Excel tables with
   a style name), and `protection`. Workbook-level `defined_names`
   maps names to refs. Cell objects also take `hyperlink` and `note`.
   Typed values: JSON numbers/bools
   pass through; dates use `{"value": "2026-01-31", "type": "date"}`.
   Number formats are Excel format strings: currency `"$#,##0.00"`,
   percent `"0.0%"`, date `"yyyy-mm-dd"`.
2. **Formulas**: set with `"formula": "SUM(B2:B9)"` in the spec or
   `--set "C1==SUM(A:A)"` in the editor. When writing formulas, add
   `"full_calc_on_load": true` (spec) or `--recalc` (editor); this sets
   the workbook's `fullCalcOnLoad` flag so Excel/LibreOffice recompute
   everything on open. openpyxl itself NEVER evaluates formulas.
3. **Read**: `--sheets` for inventory (names, dimensions, merged
   ranges, chart count, tables, protection, defined names),
   `--json`/`--csv` for data, `--formulas` to
   pair each formula string with its cached result, `--notes` for
   cell comments, `--names` for defined names. Cached results
   exist only if the file was last saved by a real spreadsheet app;
   files fresh from openpyxl return `null` there. To materialize
   results headlessly run `xlsx_recalc.py file.xlsx` (uses
   LibreOffice; prints `{"recalculated": false, ...}` and exits 0
   when `soffice` is absent), then reload with `--data-only`.
4. **Edit**: `xlsx_edit.py` applies renames/copies first, then
   structural row/column changes, then `--set`/`--append`. It edits in
   place unless `--out` is given — copy the file first if you need the
   original.
5. **Restructure**: for insert/delete on sheets that have formulas,
   merges, tables, or filters, use `xlsx_restructure.py` instead of
   `xlsx_edit.py`. It rewrites formula references on ALL sheets
   (absolute `$` refs, ranges, cross-sheet refs), shifts merges,
   autofilter, freeze panes, validation and conditional-format
   ranges, table refs, defined names, and row/column dimensions, then
   prints a JSON report including a `not_shifted` list. Rules and
   limits: `references/restructuring.md`.
6. **CSV interop**: `csv_to_xlsx.py` infers int/float/bool/ISO-date
   per cell and styles the header row; `xlsx_to_csv.py` writes ISO
   dates and blank strings for empty cells. Both default to UTF-8 and
   accept `--encoding` (e.g. `utf-8-sig` for Excel-friendly BOM,
   `cp1252` for legacy Windows exports).

## Converting to PDF

LibreOffice converts headlessly (also works for CSV export of a single
sheet):

```bash
soffice --headless --convert-to pdf report.xlsx --outdir out/
soffice --headless --convert-to csv report.xlsx --outdir out/  # 1st sheet only
```

Only the first sheet lands in a CSV; for other sheets use
`xlsx_to_csv.py --sheet NAME`. If `soffice` is missing, install
LibreOffice or hand the file to the user unconverted.

## Pitfalls

- **openpyxl does not calculate.** Formula results are available only
  via `load_workbook(path, data_only=True)` and only when the file was
  previously saved by Excel/LibreOffice. Otherwise you get `None`.
- **`xlsx_edit.py` insert/delete does not shift references** (raw
  openpyxl behavior). Use `xlsx_restructure.py`, which does — but even
  it cannot move chart anchors, images, or conditional-format RULE
  formulas; read its JSON report's `not_shifted` list and
  `references/restructuring.md`.
- **Sheet protection is NOT security.** `--protect` sets the standard
  xlsx sheet-protection hash: it signals "don't edit this" to
  well-behaved apps and nothing more. Anyone can strip it by editing
  the zip's XML or unchecking it in LibreOffice. Never rely on it for
  confidentiality or integrity; it does not encrypt anything.
- **`data_only=True` then save** silently discards all formulas
  (cached values replace them). Never save a workbook loaded that way
  unless that is the goal.
- **Loading strips charts/images**: openpyxl does not round-trip
  charts, so editing a charted workbook and saving drops the charts.
  Re-add charts after editing, or avoid re-saving charted files.
- **CSV locale traps**: always pass explicit encodings (the scripts
  already do) and remember European CSVs often use `;` delimiters and
  decimal commas — use `--delimiter ';'` and expect strings like
  `"12,5"` to stay strings.
- **Dates are datetimes**: Excel stores dates as serial numbers;
  openpyxl returns `datetime`/`date` objects. Dumps here emit ISO
  strings.
- Sheet names are capped at 31 chars and reject `[ ] : * ? / \`.

## Verification

- After creating: `xlsx_read.py out.xlsx --sheets` and confirm sheet
  names, dimensions, merged ranges, and chart counts match intent.
- Dump data with `--json` and compare against the source values.
- After edits: re-dump the touched range; if formulas were written,
  confirm `--formulas` lists them and that `--recalc` was applied.
- After `xlsx_restructure.py`: read its JSON report, then re-run
  `--formulas` and `--sheets` to confirm references and ranges landed
  where expected.
- For a full visual check, open in LibreOffice:
  `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf out.xlsx` and inspect the PDF.

# MCP Browser Automation (BrowserClaw)

Configure Hermes Agent to connect to local browsers that expose MCP endpoints via HTTP/StreamableHTTP (e.g., BrowserClaw at `http://127.0.0.1:9010/mcp`).

## When to Use

- You have a local browser (BrowserClaw, Playwright MCP, etc.) running an MCP server on HTTP
- You want to use browser automation tools as native Hermes tools
- You prefer MCP over `browser_exec` for tighter integration

## Prerequisites

- **mcp Python package with HTTP support** — `pip install --upgrade mcp`
- Browser MCP server running and accessible (default BrowserClaw: `http://127.0.0.1:9010/mcp`)

## Configuration

Add to `~/.hermes/config.yaml` under `mcp_servers`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  browserclaw:
    url: "http://127.0.0.1:9010/mcp"
    timeout: 180
    connect_timeout: 60
```

**Restart Hermes Agent** after editing — MCP discovery runs only at startup.

## Tool Naming

Tools are registered with prefix `mcp__browserclaw__` (double underscore):

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `mcp__browserclaw__tabs` | List/create/close tabs |
| `mcp__browserclaw__navigate` | Navigate (url, back, forward, reload) |
| `mcp__browserclaw__read` | Extract page as markdown |
| `mcp__browserclaw__screenshot` | Capture screenshot |
| `mcp__browserclaw__act` | Click, type, hover, select |
| `mcp__browserclaw__evaluate` | Execute JavaScript |
| `mcp__browserclaw__wait` | Wait for text/element |
| `mcp__browserclaw__grep` | Search page content |
| `mcp__browserclaw__pdf` | Save as PDF |
| `mcp__browserclaw__download` | Download files |
| `mcp__browserclaw__upload` | Upload files |
| `mcp__browserclaw__name_session` | Rename session |

## Common Workflow

```python
# 1. Create a new tab with purpose (returns page_id)
mcp__browserclaw__tabs(action="new", purpose="extrair título artigo", url="https://example.com")  # → page_id

# 2. Navigate (if not done in step 1)
mcp__browserclaw__navigate(page=page_id, action="url", url="https://example.com")

# 3. Interact
mcp__browserclaw__act(page=page_id, action="click", ref="e1")
mcp__browserclaw__act(page=page_id, action="type", ref="e2", text="query")

# 4. Extract — ABA FECHA AUTOMATICAMENTE APÓS EXTRAÇÃO BEM-SUCEDIDA (salvo keep_open=true)
mcp__browserclaw__read(page=page_id)
mcp__browserclaw__screenshot(page=page_id)

# 5. Para fluxos multi-step, use keep_open=true na criação:
mcp__browserclaw__tabs(action="new", purpose="preencher formulário", keep_open=true, url="https://form.com")
# ... múltiplos navigate/act/read ...
# Feche explicitamente ou deixe cleanup_tabs()/troca de sessão limpar:
mcp__browserclaw__tabs(action="close", page=page_id)
```

### Limpeza Automática
- **Pós-extração:** abas sem `keep_open` fecham sozinhas após `read`/`grep`/`screenshot`/`evaluate`
- **Troca de tarefa:** `name_session name="nova-tarefa"` fecha abas da tarefa anterior sem `keep_open`
- **Limite LRU:** máx 5 abas simultâneas sem `keep_open` — excedentes fecham a mais antiga
- **Timeout:** abas inativas >10min sem `keep_open` fecham no próximo `tabs list`

Ver `browserclaw-usage` → "Gerenciamento Automático de Abas" e `references/tab-lifecycle-management.md` para detalhes completos.

## Após Configurar → Operar com `browserclaw-usage`

Esta skill cobre apenas a **configuração da conexão MCP**. Para operar o BrowserClaw (abas, snapshots, actions, extração, workflows, pitfalls), use a skill **`browserclaw-usage`** — ela é o manual operacional completo.

```bash
# Carregar a skill de operação
skill_view(name="browserclaw-usage")
```

## Troubleshooting

### "MCP server requires HTTP transport but mcp.client.streamable_http is not available"

```bash
pip install --upgrade mcp
```
Then restart Hermes.

### Tools not appearing after config

1. Check `hermes doctor` → "Tool Availability" section
2. Check logs: `hermes logs agent -n 200 --component tools | grep -i mcp`
3. Verify server responds: `curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" http://127.0.0.1:9010/mcp`
4. Restart Hermes fully (close + open)

### "page X is not owned by this agent"

Always create a new tab first with `tabs action="new"` — the initial `chrome://newtab/` page is not agent-owned.

Use this as a conservative normalization guide when exporting recent post metrics.

## Post identity

- `post_url` — canonical post URL.

- `Visualizações` -> `views`
- `Alcance` -> `reach`
- `Curtidas` -> `likes`
- `Comentários` -> `comments`
- `Compartilhamentos` -> `shares`
- `Salvamentos` -> `saves`

- `Toques no link externo` -> `external_link_taps`
- `Seguidores` / `Não seguidores` -> keep as split fields under the parent metric when the page shows a breakdown.

- `document.body.innerText` is often more useful than the accessibility snapshot for Instagram post pages.
